newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope presides at Palm Sunday celebrations.
newsitem.headline: Pope presides at Palm Sunday celebrations.

text.p: Pope John Paul led the world's Roman Catholics in Palm Sunday celebrations, starting a hectic Holy Week of pre-Easter activities that will test the stamina of the 76-year-old Pontiff.
Tens of thousands of people in St Peter's Square waved palm and olive branches as the 76-year-old Pope was driven in an open jeep to an altar on the steps of Christendom's largest church.
Palm Sunday commemorates Christ's triumphant entry into Jerusalem a week before his arrest, death by crucifixion and resurrection.
In his homily during a mass, the Pontiff, dressed in red and gold vestments, recounted the Biblical story of Christ's passion and death.
Palm Sunday is also one of the two days the Roman Catholic Church is marking its World Day of Youth this year. The Pope is due to travel to Paris in August for the second celebration.

The Pope appeared in relatively good form during Sunday's three-hour-service. He has suffered a spate of health problems in recent years, most recently in October, when he had surgery to remove his appendix.
Sunday marked the start of a busy week for the Pope leading up to Easter, the most important day in the Christian liturgical calendar.

On Thursday, he will preside at a vespers service in the Rome basilica of St John Lateran during which he will wash and kiss the feet of 12 men in a gesture commemorating Christ's humilty towards his apostles on the night before he died.
He will lead three services on Good Friday, the day Christians commemorate Christ's crucifixion, including a candlelight Via Crucis (way of the cross) procession around the Colosseum in Rome.
The Pope's Holy Week activities culminate on Easter Sunday, when he says mass in St Peter's Square and delivers his twice-yearly "Urbi et Orbi" (to the city and the world) message and blessing.
